title: Resource-efficient quantum-selected configuration interaction for molecular properties
authors: Suprava Sahoo, Abdul Kalam, Kenji Sugisaki, V. S. Prasannaa, B. P. Das
abstract: The quantum-selected configuration interaction identifies important determinantal basis functions through real-time evolution of a reference wavefunction and diagonalizing the Hamiltonian matrix in the resulting selected subspace. However, implementing the full electronic Hamiltonian on noisy quantum devices leads to rapidly increasing circuit complexity, limiting its scalability. To address this issue, we identify the dominant fermionic excitation operators and perform reference-state fidelity loss analysis to construct a compact Hamiltonian, reducing computational overhead while retaining high precision. Applied to Group IIIA monofluorides (BF, AlF, GaF, InF, and TlF), the proposed framework achieves a near-quadratic improvement in Hamiltonian-term scaling, enabling resource-efficient simulations. We employ this framework to compute the relativistic ground-state energies and permanent electric dipole moments (PDMs) of the systems under consideration. After validating the framework via simulations, we demonstrate hardware execution for AlF and TlF on the IBM Marrakesh processor using active spaces of up to 20 qubits. For a 20-qubit TlF system, the reduced Hamiltonian yields a reduction of higher than $ 98\%$ in both circuit depth and two-qubit gate counts, with the resulting PDMs from quantum hardware matching complete active space configuration interaction values within $99.99\%$. These results demonstrate the scalability of this approach on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.
summary: The paper introduces an $	ext{eos-QSCI}$ method to calculate molecular properties by drastically reducing the complexity of the electronic Hamiltonian. This is achieved by screening out negligible Pauli operator terms based on reference-state fidelity loss, leading to massive resource savings in circuit depth and gate counts compared to full methods. The results confirm that this approach enables accurate simulations for molecules like $	ext{TlF}$ on near-term quantum hardware.
main_problem: The primary challenge is simulating quantum many-body systems, like molecules, for properties beyond ground-state energies while overcoming the exponential scaling limitations of exact electronic structure methods.
main_result: The proposed resource-efficient framework achieves near-quadratic improvements in Hamiltonian term scaling and demonstrates that calculations on NISQ devices maintain high accuracy (e.g., PDM matching within 99.99% of full CI).
method: The authors developed an effective Pauli Operator Sorting-based Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction ($	ext{eos-QSCI}$) method that prunes the Hamiltonian by retaining only dominant terms based on reference-state fidelity loss.
model_or_system: The study applies this framework to Group IIIA monofluorides (BF, AlF, GaF, InF, TlF), using the Dirac–Coulomb Hamiltonian within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation for electronic structure calculations.
key_observables: Ground-state energies and Permanent Electric Dipole Moments (PDMs); quantum resource metrics include circuit depth and two-qubit gate counts.
important_parameters: The fidelity loss threshold ($c.w.(K) \gtrsim 0.99$) is used to construct the compact Hamiltonian; system sizes up to 20 qubits are tested.
main_assumptions: The method relies on approximating the full electronic Hamiltonian by retaining only terms whose contribution, measured via reference-state fidelity loss, exceeds a certain threshold.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three phases of the $	ext{eos-QSCI}$ workflow: Hamiltonian construction (screening/Jordan-Wigner), time-evolution circuit building using Sets of Commuting Observables (SCOs), and hardware execution results. Tables quantify resource reductions ($	ext{HT}$, $	ext{CD}$, $	ext{CX}$) compared to full methods.
paper_structure: The paper details the problem (FCI intractability), introduces the $	ext{eos-QSCI}$ methodology through Hamiltonian screening and importance selection based on fidelity loss, presents resource scaling analyses showing super-linear advantages over full Hamiltonians, and validates the approach by calculating energies and PDMs for several Group IIIA monofluorides on simulated quantum hardware.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the scalability bottleneck in quantum chemistry simulations. By providing a systematic way to compress the Hamiltonian before circuit construction, it makes calculations of molecular properties feasible on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic workflow of the proposed eos-QSCI method. PHASE I: Construction of the truncated Hamiltonian through reference-state-based screening of non-contributing terms followed by the Jordan–Wigner transformation. PHASE II: Time-evolution circuit construction via fidelity loss and cumulative-weight-based Hamiltonian-term selection and grouping into sets of commuting observables (SCOs). PHASE III: Pipeline optimization, quantum hardware execution, and classical post-processing to obtain the ground-state energy and wavefunction.

Figure 2. Absolute energy deviations, ∆E = |Eeos-QSCI − ECASCI|, for Group IIIA monofluorides obtained with eos- QSCI for active spaces corresponding to (a) 12, (b) 14, (c) 18, and (d) 20 qubits. The vertical axis is shown on a logarithmic scale.
